text:
meena-support: Customer reports sudden 401 invalid_api_key after rotating keys this morning. They say they updated the K8s Secret but app still getting 401. Customer provided a sample curl and a Redwood request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Can infra confirm whether the request hit our edge and which key was seen? :eyes:

devon: Can you paste the curl you ran (with the header redacted) and the exact timestamp / request-id? Also which cluster/provider and how you mounted the secret (k8s secret vs secrets-store CSI vs env)?

meena-support: Here's the curl (redacted):

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Response: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Body: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found or revoked"}

Request id: req_0a1b2c3d
Cluster: gke-prod-uswest (customer-managed nodepool)
Secret mount: using secrets-store.csi.k8s.io (external vault provider)
They say they rotated key at 09:12 UTC and updated Vault -> synced to secret provider at 09:15, but app logs still show 401 between 09:20-09:40.

raj-infra: Quick hypothesis: CSI provider (or the node-level cache) still serving the old file in the pod filesystem until the driver syncs or the pod is restarted. There are two common gotchas: (1) provider sync interval / syncer not triggered, (2) pod rollout strategy OnDelete so pods weren't recreated. Ask customer to check the mounted file timestamp inside the pod: `stat /etc/secrets/redwood_key` and `ls -l /var/lib/kubelet/pods/.../volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/...`

lucy-cs: Also confirm the pod's env: some apps load the key into environment on container start and never re-read the file. If they updated the file under the mount but the process cached it in env var, it will continue using the old key until restart.

meena-support: I asked them to exec into the pod and run the stat and cat. They returned:

```
$ kubectl exec -n prod myapp-5d7f8 -- cat /etc/secrets/redwood_key
old-key-abcdef123456
$ stat /etc/secrets/redwood_key
Access: 2026-03-10 09:13:27.000000000 +0000
Modify: 2026-03-10 09:13:27.000000000 +0000
Change: 2026-03-10 09:13:27.000000000 +0000
```

They claim Vault/secret provider reported a sync at 09:15 but the file on node shows 09:13. So it's clear the file wasn't updated on that pod.

devon: Can ops check our ingress logs to see which api_key string we received for req_0a1b2c3d? If it matches the old-key-abcdef... then it's definitely a pod-level stale file.

ops-bot: Ingress trace for req_0a1b2c3d -> forwarded request header Authorization bearer hashed to key fingerprint: sha256:7fa3... (maps to old-key-abcdef123456). Route backed to cluster gke-prod-uswest -> node ip 10.128.3.45 -> pod myapp-5d7f8

raj-infra: OK confirmed. Root cause: secrets-store CSI driver did not update the file inside that pod. Likely because the provider's syncer had not run on that node, or the pod was scheduled on a node with the old cached mount. Two mitigations: (A) restart the pods (kubectl rollout restart deploy/myapp) — this forces containers to read new secret into env or file; (B) patch syncer/provider to force re-pull; (C) if using OnDelete strategy, perform rolling delete to pick up new mount.

lucy-cs: Customer impact: requests failed for ~25 minutes. Recommend we document this pattern for customers using secrets-store CSI and suggest a post-rotation checklist: 1) confirm secret provider sync, 2) check mount timestamps in pods, 3) restart pods if apps read secrets on startup, 4) verify via an authenticated curl and confirm request-id.

jordan-customer: I did `kubectl rollout restart deploy/myapp` and then retried the request. It succeeds now (200). Verified using req id req_0a1b2c3d-2 (new one). Thanks.

meena-support: Great — closing loop with the customer. Root cause: rotated key updated in Vault but the secrets-store CSI mount on the running pod still had the old file (driver/node-level caching + app reading secret on startup). Resolution steps we recommended: restart deployment or node-level sync, and add the post-rotation checklist above. Filing this as an operational note for support docs. :white_check_mark:

raj-infra: Optional follow-up: we can add a short troubleshooting snippet to our docs for "401 after rotation" covering CSI providers and common Kubernetes pitfalls (env vs file, OnDelete rollout). I'll open a short PR to docs repos.

meena-support: Thanks team — closing the thread. If customer asks for automation next time, suggest using a pre-rotation hook that triggers a rolling restart or a post-rotation webhook to signal the app to reload secrets if it supports SIGHUP-based reloads.
